answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy binds identities to thermodynamic telemetry at coastal estuaries. Sensor nodes log erratic salinity and temperature gradients where runoff from a walnut grove empties into the ocean. Because adversaries cannot forge these chaotic fluid interactions, each fake identity requires fabricating and anchoring a dedicated marine probe. However, severe storm surges periodically wash out estuary gradients, temporarily disrupting legitimate verification.
